To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

jitter-induced P/G voltage noise in CMOS circuits can be modeled by using the statistical properties of P/G noise and that the PLL timing jitter can be predicted in response to VCO phase noise, which is caused by the P/G noise.

(a) the phase noise of a VCO in a PLL is a function of the statistical properties (mean and variance) of the P/G noise; (b) the timing jitter of the PLL output is a function of its VCO's phase noise; (c) the P/G noise can be reduced by using a low noise VCO; and (d) the PLL jitter can be minimized by increasing the PLL loop bandwidth and/or by increasing the loop filter's bandwidth.

the power/ground jitter-induced noise in CMOS phase- locked loops (PLLs) can be modeled as a stochastic process with a Gaussian distribution, that the phase noise of a voltage-controlled oscillator ( VCO) is a function of the statistical properties (variance and mean) of the power/ ground (P/G) voltage noise, and finally, that the timing jitter of PLLs is a function of VCO phase noise, and hence a function of the power/ grounding voltage noise.
